- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce the forecast peak by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid overcorrecting downward; add 1–3% to prevent premature bottoming.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), model should not overpredict further decline.
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, reduce the spike magnitude by 10–20% to account for sentiment lag.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates > 3% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not just last 18 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.5) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by reducing volatility in 3–5 day windows.
